dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are you visiting me at this hour... not trying to buy intel from me, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: I've been very busy lately, you know. A major client has booked two full weeks of my time.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Yes. I can't disclose any details, but suffice to say he's exceptionally rich — so don't even think about trying to out-bid him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but... shouldn't informants only share their intel with one person?

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Maybe in an ideal world, but business is business at the end of the day, and if you only have one partnership, you'll eventually starve to death.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: The Knights of Favonius are sticklers for principle, but even they have a practice of obtaining intelligence from a minimum of two sources during large-scale operations.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: They've suffered badly from incomplete intelligence in the past. That's why people like me are so important — I'm there when they need the extra support, and I'm free to find other work when they don't.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Here's an analogy. Imagine the Abyss Order has set up an ambush in the wilderness — a single scouting team is unlikely to detect it.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Next thing you know, a knight on patrol passes by, completely unsuspecting, when suddenly "Waah!" A monster jumps out and clubs him over the head with a "bish" and a "bash."

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Well, I just thought they might make the whole thing sound more realistic.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, not even close! Monsters go "Yaah!" not "Waah!" And it's a "swish" and a "smash," not a "bish" and a "bash"!

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Don't be so single-minded... You can think what you want, of course, but it can't hurt to keep my version on file as alternative intel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Hmm, guess that kinda makes sense...

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Anyway, to get back to the point... buyers are demanding multiple sources, and it's only fair that informants are free to serve multiple clients too, don't you think?

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Of course I do. All work is just selling your labor hours. The intelligence business is no different.
